I am an 80-year-old farmer in the North East, and I have been growing beans and legumes on this land for many decades. I will use the cowpea seeds I saved from last year's harvest and spread some cow manure that my children gathered from our animals, because I know this keeps the soil good for legumes. I will not buy chemical fertilizer or spray for pests—those things cost too much money, and at my age I cannot easily get to the agro-dealer or carry those chemicals. My sons and grandchildren will do most of the planting, weeding, and harvesting, but I will hire a few young men from the village to help with the heavy clearing and the harvest when the work is too much for my family alone.
